why.raw stays append-only: an edited raw file destroys the only thing a rebuild can restore from; flipping `processed` is the one sanctioned edit, and deletion only under a declared retention obligation
why.usage/log.md row appended: the friction field is the whole improvement flywheel; a skill that skips it under pressure makes corp-os-improve blind
why.derived-layer writes have a proposal beh: a proposal that lives only in chat dies with the session and leaves no record of what the gate saw -- the declines especially, which are the only trace of what someone chose not to know
why.the shipped script this OS predates is i: corp-os-configure's retention path calls this at the OS path and fails against an OS that does not have it. An upgrade run that leaves it missing has not upgraded anything
why.the stale counter copy was replaced: this is the copy that counts a single-file layer wrong. It is the entire reason the upgrade path exists, and it differs by content while looking fine by date
why.the recorded version moved: an OS that does not record which version it is on cannot be told it is behind, so the next run has to rediscover everything from disk shape alone
why.the run closed its own books: every failing conformance check in this suite has been the last step of a run; log_run.py exists so this one is not the exception
why.the registry migration was NOT performed: moving someone's files is a migration, not bookkeeping. upgrade_os.py names it and refuses; corp-os-configure enumerates and asks first. A run that quietly moves the registry has collapsed the one distinction this skill is built around -- and it is more tempting here than anywhere, because the fix is one mv and the person did say to bring the folder in line
why.no source material was touched: an upgrade has no business in the append-only layer
why.the outstanding migration is named rathe: leaving the migration alone is a legitimate answer; leaving it alone without saying so is not, because the person now believes their OS is current when its index is still under-counting
